name: Vasopressin
executiveSummary: Antidiuretic hormone at vasopressor doses. Adult septic shock: fixed **0.03 U/min** (range **0.01–0.04 U/min**) as norepinephrine adjunct. Pediatrics: **0.0005–0.002 U/kg/min** (**0.03–0.12 U/kg/h**). No rapid bolus unless protocol.
indications:
## Indications

- Refractory vasodilatory shock / sepsis adjunct (Surviving Sepsis).
- Central diabetes insipidus and variceal GI bleeding: **different regimens and higher doses** — do not confuse with shock dosing.

## Precautions

- Digital, mesenteric, coronary ischemia; relative hyponatremia; ↓ cardiac output if excessive afterload.
- Central line preferred. Does not replace volume or antibiotics.
- Common ampoules: **20 U/mL**.

> In shock, “low fixed” doses; above 0.04 U/min rarely helps and increases ischemia.

adulto.dose: Septic shock: **0.03 U/min** continuous IV (alternative titration **0.01–0.04 U/min**). Varices (other regimen): often **0.2–0.4 U/min** — hepatology/GI protocol only.
adulto.administration: Dilute in NS/D5W (usual max conc. **1 U/mL**); continuous pump.
adulto.notes: Monitor BP, lactate, peripheral perfusion, and urine output.

pediatrico.dose: Refractory shock: **0.0005–0.002 U/kg/min** (approx. **0.03–0.12 U/kg/h**); some protocols up to **0.15 U/kg/h** — ID/ICU.
pediatrico.notes: Diluted: discard ~18 h room temp / ~24 h refrigerated (card).

adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Peripheral/mesenteric ischemia, hypertension, bradycardia, arrhythmias, hyponatremia, skin necrosis if extravasation.
